messages.author: 578d63f4e20ca975
messages.subject: Bayesint Problem
parts:
Has anyone had any problems running the function bayesint()? I keep getting this error:

> CIchr1 <- bayesint(F2.out1, chr = 2)
Error in bayesint(F2.out1, chr = 2) : Chromosome misspecified.

But only on the earlier chromosomes, for 10 onwards it worked fine. I saw in the documentation that it says:

chr A chromosome ID (if input results are from scanone (should have length 1).

I'm not sure what length 1 means, and if that is the issue or not. Has anyone had similar issues, do you possibly have an idea of what might be going wrong here?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Bayesint Problem
parts:
Likely the F2.out1 object doesn't contain a chromosome "2".

Check unique(F2.out1[,1]) for the chromosomes.

Regarding "length 1", that means that you can provide just one chromosome, rather than a vector of multiple chromosomes.

karl

messages.author: 578d63f4e20ca975
messages.subject: Re: Bayesint Problem
parts:
I worked it out, it was basically that numbers 1-9 had a space infront of them somehow, thus if I used " 1", instead of just 1, it would work. 

Thank you for your help!
